material_sources.locator: PMC11647717; Results and Discussion; Figures 1-3 and Tables 1-4
observations: Regulatory-site inhibitor structures reported for compounds 1, 2, 7 and 13: 9GJN, 9GK6, 9GJS and 9GKE.
Compound 1 inhibits recombinant enzyme but lacks measurable cellular inhibition in the reported assay.
Compound 13 reported enzyme pIC50 8.6 and cellular antigen-presentation pIC50 7.7.
Antigen-presentation readout is functional cellular activity, not a direct intracellular occupancy measurement.
Compound 7 ERAP2 and IRAP measurements use different substrates and n=1; selectivity ratios require contextual assessment.
material_sources.provisional_impact: Changes available chemical matter and structure landscape; does not by itself establish axSpA efficacy or direct cellular engagement.

observations: Ten common allotypes characterized using recombinant enzyme; population analysis used 2504 individuals.
Enzyme activity rankings depend on substrate; up to 60-fold efficiency difference reported for YTAFTIPSI.
GSK849 activates small-substrate hydrolysis but inhibits the longer YTAFTIPSI substrate; inhibitor response also varies by allotype.
Different enzyme concentrations used for allotypes in inhibition assays; these conditions must accompany measurements.
material_sources.provisional_impact: Supports genotype- and substrate-matched assay design; generic ERAP1 activity is insufficient as a context-free readout.

material_sources.reported_not_independently_verified: Corilagin direct interaction with ERAP1 at cellular and protein levels and reversal of HLA-B27 model phenotypes.
material_sources.required: Full methods, figures, supplements, engagement assay modality, concentration and exposure matching, viability controls, genetic controls and selectivity conditions.
material_sources.provisional_impact: Potentially material for the current engagement uncertainty; neither resolved nor dismissed without methods.

material_sources.required: Full methods, figures and supplements; binding versus cellular engagement distinction, active exposures, genetic controls and assay comparability.
